| [LIT-2312](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2312.md) v4 | The vision of autonomic computing | Kephart and Chess (2003), The vision of autonomic computing. A programmatic statement of IBM's autonomic-computing agenda: computing systems that manage themselves "given high-level objectives from administrators". It sets out four aspects of self-management (configuration, optimization, healing, protection), proposes that autonomic systems be collections of autonomic elements each consisting of managed elements and an autonomic manager, and lists engineering and scientific challenges: element life cycles, service relationships negotiated between elements, security and trust, the specification of goals by humans, emergent behaviour, robustness, multi-agent learning, negotiation theory and statistical modelling. | [LIT-2333](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2333.md) v2 | Metamorphic Testing: A Review of Challenges and Opportunities | Tsong Yueh Chen, Fei-Ching Kuo, Huai Liu, Pak-Lok Poon, Dave Towey, T. H. Tse and Zhi Quan Zhou (2018), ACM Computing Surveys 51(1), article 4, DOI 10.1145/3143561. A review by the originators of metamorphic testing: where no practical oracle checks one output, a program is checked against metamorphic relations, necessary properties of the target algorithm across two or more related inputs and their outputs. It formalizes the relations, corrects four common misreadings, and is explicit that the method alleviates the oracle problem and "can never completely solve it", since the relations are necessary, not sufficient. | [LIT-2479](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2479.md) v3 | COPE - Automating Coupled Evolution of Metamodels and Models | Herrmannsdoerfer, Benz and Juergens (2009), COPE - Automating Coupled Evolution of Metamodels and Models. When a modeling language's metamodel changes, the existing models must be migrated. The paper calls this pairing "coupled evolution". **The requirements study.** An earlier study of two industrial metamodel histories found: - about half the changes were metamodel-only; - more than three quarters of the coupled changes were metamodel-independent, so they could be reused; - the rest were metamodel-specific; - none were model-specific. This yields two requirements: reuse and expressiveness. **COPE's answer.** A language evolves through a sequence of coupled transactions, each pairing a metamodel adaptation with its model migration. There are two kinds: - **Reusable** transactions, drawn from a library: rename, extract class, generalize reference, and so on. - **Custom** transactions, written in a Turing-complete language. Read for the exchange "luria experiment design". | Active — Read on 2026-11-12 ([NOTE-1811](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1811.md)) from https://wwwbroy.in.tum.de/publ/papers/ECOOP2009_herrmannsdoerfer_cope_automating_coupled.pdf. |
